tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. No. The last five commits (all on 2026-09-22) are about printer setup, but two of them go well beyond UX/UI tweaks. They also add new printer-connection behavior and touch OrcaSlicer-owned files. Going back a few more days, the commits cover unrelated areas too.

**Commits since the printer conversation panel was merged (288b9f0dd7, 2026-09-19), newest first:**

| Commit | What it is | Printer setup UX/UI tweak? |
|---|---|---|
| 886098514b Fix Home UI test role query for TypeScript build | One-line test fix | Test fix only |
| 9f739dccf2 Keep printer connection help available and preserve its provider | UI changes, plus new behavior: a runtime override that picks which printer connection provider to use, set through `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent`. It adds 10 lines to the upstream files `GUI_App.cpp`/`.hpp`. It also removes the "Add credentials" commands from `SetupCommands.cpp`. | **Partly.** A real behavior change in an upstream-owned file. |
| 2a07ec0fc7 Give printer setup a focused workspace | Layout, a new design token, and styles | Yes |
| 4d4f9e466b Replace printer summary card with conversational setup guidance | Removes a summary card and changes the model's instructions | Yes (UI plus prompt wording) |
| 67577ad993 Add optional printer connection after saving named printers | A new feature: "connect later" actions on Home, reuse of Bambu and print-host (network printer) connection settings, and saved printers kept when a connection fails. About 230 lines in `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` and about 140 in `PrinterConversation.cpp`. | **No.** A feature, not a tweak. |
| b361b84773 Skip automatic setup wizard in JusPrin shell | Stops Orca's first-run setup wizard from opening at startup when the JusPrin shell is active. It adds a flag check to the upstream file `GUI_App.cpp`. | Related (first-run printer setup), but a startup behavior change |
| a7bb15ef9d Configure Codex sandbox mode | One line in `.codex/config.toml` | **No.** Tooling config. |
| ee1bb889a2 Give the Prepare canvas its tools and values back, in a corner row | A new viewport toolbar and value panel (about 2,000 lines), including small additions to the upstream files `GLCanvas3D` and `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp` | **No.** Unrelated canvas work. |
| a975c79be6 Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, … Bambu spool simulation | Mostly polish of the printer panel, plus fake Bambu printer spool simulation for testing | Mostly yes, plus test tooling |
| 86d71f3e2c, e00729f58e | An AGENTS.md rule about temporary docs, and removal of a handoff doc | **No.** Repo housekeeping. |

**If you're thinking of reviewing or squashing these as one "printer setup polish" batch:**
- Pull out ee1bb889a2 (canvas toolbar) and a7bb15ef9d (Codex config). Neither is about printer setup.
- Review 67577ad993 and 9f739dccf2 as features, not tweaks. Both change how printers connect, not just how setup looks.
- Three commits touch OrcaSlicer-owned files, which the fork has to re-resolve at every rebase: b361b84773 and 9f739dccf2 (`GUI_App.cpp`/`.hpp`) and ee1bb889a2 (`GLCanvas3D`, `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`). Only 9f739dccf2's message includes the rebase evidence that `fork-stewardship.md` asks for.

The working tree also has a large set of uncommitted printer-panel changes (for example, `PrinterConnection.tsx` is deleted and `replyChoices.ts` is new). I didn't include those because they aren't commits yet.

content.text:
No, not all of them. Of the 26 upstream lines, two hooks have no fork-side alternative for their goal. The printer-agent override is not needed to connect a printer; it only serves an extra requirement. Part of the gizmo change is dead code.

| Change | Needed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Wizard flag (`GUI_App`, 4 lines) | **Yes** | Orca opens the wizard when the config file didn't exist at startup (`m_app_conf_exists`, a private field) or when only default printers are installed. Neither can be changed from outside Orca's code without a hack, such as writing a config file early. |
| Printer-agent override (`GUI_App`, 10 lines) | **No, not for connecting** | See below. |
| Canvas overlay callback (`GLCanvas3D`, 6 lines) | **Yes, given the design** | `GLCanvas3D::render()` has no hook for drawing inside its ImGui frame (ImGui is the canvas's own UI layer). The alternative is native wx controls on top of the OpenGL canvas. I didn't test that, but I'd expect it to be unreliable across platforms. |
| `reset_rotation()` wrapper | **Yes** | It depends on `m_init_rotation_scale_tran`, which is private. The fork can't reproduce it. |
| `reset_scale()` wrapper | **Not strictly** | The fork could get the same result through public calls: `Plater::TakeSnapshot` plus `on_change("scale", axis, 100)` for each axis. That means copying 3 lines instead of adding 1 line upstream. Reasonable either way. |
| `reset_position()` wrapper | **No, it's unused** | Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` or `tests/` calls it. This line can be removed. |

**The printer-agent override, in detail.** Commit 67577ad993, one commit earlier, already connected Bambu printers with zero upstream changes. It created the Bambu agent with the public `NetworkAgentFactory` and installed it with `NetworkAgent::set_printer_agent`. Commit 9f739dccf2 replaced that with the override for one reason: to stop Orca from swapping the agent back when the printer profile changes. Orca re-picks the agent from the selected printer profile in `Tab::on_presets_changed` and in the OK handler of the physical printer dialog.

That only matters when a **non-Bambu** printer profile is selected. For a Bambu profile, Orca already picks the Bambu agent, and it handles the fake Bambu agent too. So the override exists only for this rule: "keep talking to a Bambu printer while the user has a non-Bambu profile selected." That rule is a product decision, not a technical necessity. Stock Orca deliberately makes the connection follow the selected profile.

The override also has a side effect I haven't tested. Nothing clears it until the shell is torn down. So after one Bambu connection, selecting a Moonraker or OctoPrint profile would keep the Bambu agent instead of Orca's own agent. That would skip Orca's automatic device selection for network printers (`select_machine`).

**Suggestions:**
1. Delete the unused `reset_position()` wrapper now.
2. Decide whether a Bambu connection should persist while a non-Bambu profile is selected. If not, go back to 67577ad993's approach, which needed no upstream change, and drop the override and its rebase risk. If it should, keep the override, but define when it gets cleared and test switching to a Moonraker profile.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
---
name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

```sh
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target OrcaSlicer agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness -- -j6
build/arm64/tests/agent/RelWithDebInfo/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_bridge_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp -v
npm --prefix src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI test
build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --mcp-bridge
```

The same run on the Windows verification machine, where the generator is Visual Studio and there is no `python3`:

```sh
cmake --build build --config Release --target OrcaSlicer agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness -- -m
build/tests/agent/Release/agent_bridge_tests.exe --order rand --warn NoAssertions
npm --prefix src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI test
build/tests/shell/Release/shell_integration_harness.exe --mcp-bridge
```

The workspace adapter harness runs there too, and passes (617 checks, exit 0, as of 2026-09-17). Put the app's `src\Release` on `PATH`, or the exe cannot load the `api-ms-win-crt` DLLs, and read the exit code with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell:

content.text:
I made both changes in a new worktree. The fork now adds 15 lines to upstream OrcaSlicer files instead of 26, and all three shell harness modes I ran pass. Nothing is committed yet; the worktree is at `.claude/worktrees/drop-upstream-extras` on branch `claude/drop-upstream-extras`, cut from 886098514b.

**Upstream changes removed (11 lines):**
- **Unused gizmo wrapper:** deleted the `reset_position()` line from `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`.
- **Printer-agent override:** deleted from `GUI_App.hpp` (the field, its comment and `#include <utility>`) and from `switch_printer_agent()` in `GUI_App.cpp`.

What's left upstream: the 4-line wizard flag, the 6-line canvas overlay callback, and the `reset_rotation()` and `reset_scale()` wrappers.

**Fork-side replacements:**
- **Connecting a Bambu printer:** `OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection` again creates the Bambu agent and installs it directly, using public calls, as 67577ad993 did. I added one line that commit didn't have: it refreshes the sidebar's printer dropdowns, which Orca's own agent switch also does.
- **Shell teardown:** `ShellController::uninstall()` now always calls `switch_printer_agent()`, so the printer profile chooses the agent again. It does nothing when the agent already matches the profile.
- **Harness:** the check "explicit provider survives profile re-evaluation" became "profile re-evaluation replaces the connection provider" plus "connecting again reinstalls it". I also removed a stock-mode check that only tested the deleted field.

**Test results** (a fresh RelWithDebInfo build, with the web pages built):

| Harness mode | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--printer-setup` (runs the fake-Bambu connection flow and the new checks) | 124 | all pass |
| default (includes the shell uninstall checks) | 412 | all pass |
| `--stock` | 24 | all pass (25 before, minus the removed check) |

**Behavior change to accept or reject:** you now lose a Bambu printer's connection when you select a non-Bambu printer profile. Before this change, the connection survived that switch. Home will show the printer's status as unknown until you reconnect, and reconnecting works; the harness checks that. This matches stock Orca. If you'd rather keep the connection, drop this branch and keep the override.

**Before landing:** your uncommitted work in the main checkout also edits `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp`, `ShellController.cpp` and `shell_harness.cpp`. It doesn't touch the lines I changed, but `shell_harness.cpp` has 320 lines of edits there, so a cherry-pick may conflict in that file.

Want me to commit it on the branch?

input.command:
git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Connect Bambu printers without patching Orca's agent switch

The fork added lines to two OrcaSlicer files that it does not need:

- GUI_App gained a printer_agent_override field, applied inside
  switch_printer_agent(), so that a Bambu connection made from Home would
  survive a change to a non-Bambu printer profile. Connecting itself never
  needed it: the Bambu agent can be created with the public
  NetworkAgentFactory and installed with NetworkAgent::set_printer_agent,
  which is what OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection does again now.
- GizmoObjectManipulation gained a reset_position() wrapper that nothing calls.

Removing both leaves 15 fork lines in upstream files instead of 26. All
removals are of fork-added lines; no upstream line is deleted or moved.
GUI_App.hpp is byte-identical to its state before 9f739dccf2.

Behavior change: selecting a non-Bambu printer profile now hands the
agent back to Orca's profile-driven choice, as stock Orca does, so a
Bambu printer's live status on Home goes stale until it is connected
again. Connecting again reinstalls the Bambu agent. Shell teardown now
always calls switch_printer_agent() so the profile picks the agent again;
the call does nothing when the agent already matches.

prepare_connection also refreshes the sidebar's preset dropdowns after
installing the agent, as switch_printer_agent() does, since the sync-AMS
button depends on the agent.

Tests: the shell harness now checks that profile re-evaluation replaces
the connection agent, that connecting again reinstalls it, and that the
reconnected printer delivers fresh data. The stock-mode check that only
guarded the removed field is gone. On a fresh macOS RelWithDebInfo build
with web pages built: --printer-setup 124/124, default 412/412,
--stock 24/24 checks pass.

Rebase check: git merge-tree against upstream/main 7ca2b9ad9c (merge base
3ffb9585d2). Before this commit GUI_App.hpp, GUI_App.cpp and GLCanvas3D.cpp
conflict; after it, GUI_App.hpp no longer conflicts. GUI_App.cpp conflicts
as a single whole-file block both before and after, so this change does not
alter it.
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s' && git status --short | wc -l

content.text:
No. My first round of testing didn't cover the behavior change properly, and the more thorough test I just ran found a bug in the commit I made (744de242a3). I don't recommend landing it as it is.

**What the first round missed:**
- **The real profile path:** the harness called Orca's agent switch directly. It never selected a profile the way a user does, which is what triggers the switch.
- **What Home shows afterward:** nothing checked the printer's status once its connection was gone.
- **Shell teardown:** nothing checked what happens to a connection that's still open when the shell is removed.

**What I added and ran** (the new checks are uncommitted in the worktree):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Selecting the Bambu printer's own profile keeps its connection | pass |
| Selecting a non-Bambu profile, through Orca's real preset selection, drops the Bambu connection | pass (expected behavior) |
| Connecting again reinstalls the Bambu connection and fresh data arrives | pass |
| Removing the shell while a Bambu connection is open gives the connection choice back to the profile | pass |
| Printer status right after the connection is dropped | **still says connected; see below** |

Overall: `--printer-setup` passed 126 of 126 checks and the default mode passed 411 of 411. Three keyboard-focus checks skipped themselves because two harness windows were open at once; that's unrelated.

**The bug:** after a non-Bambu profile is selected, the printer's status still reads as connected for 30 seconds, even though the connection is gone. The status only changes once the last message from the printer is more than 30 seconds old. That rule is shared by the printer panel and Home's printer list (`describe_device` in `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`). So for those 30 seconds Home would show "Connected", or a stale "Printing 45%", and then switch to "Status unknown". It can't happen with the override, because the override never drops the connection. I saw this in the harness state, not in the running app's UI.

The fix isn't a one-liner. The status rule would have to know whether the agent that sent a printer's data is still the active one, and Orca's device records don't store that. The obvious shortcut, "live only while a Bambu agent is active", would wrongly mark printers that talk through Orca's own agent as offline, such as Moonraker printers.

**Options:**
1. **Keep the override (my recommendation).** Revert the override removal and keep only the unused `reset_position()` deletion. The override is 10 upstream lines, but it prevents this bug and the harness already covers it. Removing it trades rebase effort for a user-visible defect plus new fork code to work around it.
2. **Keep my commit and fix the status rule.** This needs a fork-side record of which agent each device's data came from, plus a test that the status changes at once. It's more fork code than the 10 lines it saves upstream.

Should I go with option 1?

The override was added by **9f739dccf2**, "Keep printer connection help available and preserve its provider", on 2026-09-22. On `jusprin-newui`, it's the only commit that adds or removes `printer_agent_override`.

It added:
- **The upstream hook (10 lines):** the `printer_agent_override` field in `GUI_App.hpp` and the block in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent()` that applies it.
- **The fork caller:** `OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection` sets the override and calls `switch_printer_agent()`. Before this commit, it created and installed the Bambu agent directly.
- **Shell cleanup:** `ShellController` saves the override when the shell installs and restores it on uninstall or when the window is destroyed.
- **Harness checks:** "explicit provider survives profile re-evaluation" and a stock-mode check that the override is empty.

The same commit also has unrelated printer-panel changes (connection help, reconnect actions on Home, nozzle-mismatch reporting). So `git revert 9f739dccf2` would undo those as well, not just the override.

<pasted_content id="658c">
Okay now restate this problem as clearly as you can in plain English in a way that a normal software engineer can understand. Do not use jargons or stuff and tell me why and tell me your justification for choosing this solution.
3:14 PM
The problem is that choosing settings for slicing a model can also change the software used to communicate with a printer.
OrcaSlicer normally ties those choices together. Selecting a Bambu slicing profile selects the Bambu connection software. Selecting another manufacturer’s profile can replace it.
Our new flow lets you connect a saved Bambu printer without changing the slicing profile of the project you’re editing. That creates a conflict: the connection flow chooses Bambu, but a later slicing-profile change can undo that choice. A printer connection could therefore be disrupted by an action that appears unrelated to connecting or disconnecting.
I chose to make the explicit connection choice take priority. Once our connection flow chooses Bambu, later slicing-profile changes keep using the Bambu connection software. When the JusPrin interface shuts down, it restores the previous selection rule.
My justification was:

* Changing slicing settings should not silently undo a connection the user explicitly established.
* Connecting a printer should not silently change the settings of an open project.
* Using OrcaSlicer’s existing switching function avoids maintaining a second copy of its connection-management code.

The weakness is that the solution changes an application-wide rule to solve a printer-specific problem. It keeps the Bambu connection software selected across profile changes; it does not introduce independent connection management for every saved printer.
